title: Annotatio IV §.VIII: Athanasius — spiritual presence and participation; exclude the corporal
pass_a_gloss: As wholly occupied in the Commentary on the sixth chapter of John with establishing the Spiritual presence and participation of Christ’s body and blood in the Sacred Supper, the corporal presence and participation excluded: The Lord, he says, discriminated Spirit from flesh, that we might discern that the things He spoke were not carnal but spiritual: For how would His body have sufficed men for food, that it should become nourishment of the whole world? But therefore He made mention of His ascent into heaven, that He might draw them from corporal intellect and thereafter they might understand His flesh of which He had spoken as food from above, heavenly and spiritual nourishment (pneumatikēn trophēn) to be given by Himself.
pass_b_english: Athanasius (on John 6) builds spiritual presence and participation of body and blood in the Supper — corporal presence and participation shut out.
The Lord separated Spirit from flesh so we know His speech is spiritual not carnal; He named the ascension to pull them off corporal intellect toward heavenly spiritual food (pneumatikēn trophēn).
source_text: Utpote adstruendis Spiritualibus præsentiâ ac participatione corporis & sanguinis Christi in S. Cœna, exclusis præsentia & participatione corporalibus, Commentario ad sextum Joh. caput, totus occupatus: Dominus, inquit, Spiritum à carne discriminavit, ut discerneremus ea, quæ loqueretur, non carnalia esse, sed spiritualia: Quod enim hominibus corpus ejus suffecisset ad cibum, ut universi mundi alimonia fieret? Sed proptereà adscensionis suæ in cælum mentionem fecit, ut eos à corporali intellectu abstraheret ac deinde carnem suam, de qua locutus erat, cibum è supernis cælestem & spiritualem alimoniam (pneumatikēn trophēn) ab ipso donandam intelligerent.
